Count the whole stack. In the phase-out range the CDB’s 20% sits on top of income tax, payroll contributions and other income-tested benefits such as the Canada workers benefit and its disability supplement, the Canada Groceries and Essentials Benefit and provincial programs. Earnings are treated more gently than other income. Below the exemption cap a dollar of wages or self-employment income costs no CDB; above it, it costs the same as other income. The extra-income chart shows that difference.

RDSP withdrawals are excluded. Disability assistance payments from an RDSP are subtracted in adjusted family net income, so they do not reduce the CDB. RRSP and RRIF withdrawals are fully included, so the calendar year in which they are taken decides which payment period they reduce.
Small amounts are paid at once. If the monthly amount is CAD 20 or less (CAD 240 or less for the year), the whole period is paid as one lump sum on the next payment date.

The Canada Disability Benefit (CDB) is a federal monthly payment for working-age people with disabilities and low incomes, administered by Employment and Social Development Canada (ESDC). The first payments were made in July 2025. It is tax-free: ESDC says payments are not reported as income and no tax slip is issued.
The amount above the threshold is multiplied by 20% to give the annual reduction of CAD 903.40. A negative total means income is below the threshold and the maximum is paid.

The benefit is applied for, not automatic, and new recipients are paid from the month after approval. Retroactive payments can reach back up to 24 months before the application was received, but not before June 2025.
